question: Can registered elementary-loop holonomy partition a context-by-checkpoint grid into useful transported-edit patches without manufacturing structure under uniform curvature?

sectioning_rule.patch: maximal four-neighbor connected component of admitted plaquettes
sectioning_rule.coordinate: one registered coordinate transported from the lexicographically first patch node along a deterministic sorted spanning tree
sectioning_rule.worst_case_bound: maximum registered elementary-plaquette identity-loss upper bound in the patch

persistence.component_tracking: elder component survives a merge; later components receive death and merged_into receipts

audit_placement.uncertainty: 4*q*(1-q), where q is interval-implied probability of budget-clean and orientation-preserving
audit_placement.boundary_impact: one plus the number of additional measured patches the plaquette could connect

utility_gate.pass: lower endpoint of grouped bootstrap 95% CI for patch-minus-baseline utility is greater than zero for both baselines

negative_control_gate.pass: uniformly-curved fixture returns status=no_admissible_multi_patch_section and edit_count=0

noise_stability_gate.pass: registered mixed-fixture patch count lies inside the empirical 2.5%-97.5% noise-null patch-count band

claim_boundary: All gates are CPU-synthetic. A pass validates the sectioning instrument on planted receipts only and does not establish transformer edit utility.
